links.outcome: Reading grade level of original online aortic stenosis patient education materials versus recommended 6th grade
links.effect: All 21 original PEMs were above 6th-grade level; mean FRE 51.9, FKGL 9.4, GFI 11.3, SMOGI 10.1, i.e., 10th-12th grade reading level.
links.quote: Mean (SD) FRE, FKGL, GFI, and SMOGI scores of original PEMs were 51.9 (11.6), 9.4 (2.0), 11.3 (2.1), 10.1 (1.2), respectively, indicating difficult readability at the 10th–12th grade reading level (Table 1 ).

links.outcome: Readability of LLM-rewritten patient education materials versus originals
links.effect: ChatGPT-3.5 improved all four measures (FRE 76.9 vs 51.9, p<0.001), reaching ~6th-7th grade; Bard improved three of four (FRE 66.5), ~8th-9th grade; neither reached below 6th grade.
links.quote: Conversion of PEMs by ChatGPT-3.5 demonstrated significantly improved mean readability scores across all four validated measures: FRE (76.9 ± 1.2 vs 51.9 ± 11.6, p < 0.001), FKGL (5.9 ± 0.8 vs 9.4 ± 2.0, p < 0.001), GFI (7.7 ± 0.9 vs 11.3 ± 2.1, p < 0.001), and SMOGI (8.8 ± 0.6 vs 10.1 ± 1.2, p < 0.001) scores, indicating fairly easy readability at the approximately 6th–7th grade reading level.

links.effect: 21 PEMs improved, but neither chatbot reached recommended 6th-grade reading skill levels.
links.quote: Two artificial intelligence chatbots, ChatGPT and Bard, successfully improved the readability of 21 patient education materials on aortic stenosis, although neither platform reached recommended 6th-grade reading skill levels.

links.effect: ChatGPT reached approximately 6th–7th grade; Bard 8th–9th; neither below recommended 6th-grade.
links.quote: Neither platform generated PEMs written below the recommended 6th-grade reading level.

links.effect: Independent review by multiple investigators found no factual errors or inaccuracies.
links.quote: After an independent review by multiple investigators of each original PEM and the AI-generated material, there were no factual errors or inaccuracies identified.

links.outcome: Head-to-head LLM readability and conversion time
links.effect: ChatGPT had easier FRE/FKGL/GFI/SMOGI than Bard and was faster: 5.38 s ± 0.67 s vs 8.57 s ± 1.29 s.
links.quote: Compared to Bard, ChatGPT-3.5 demonstrated significantly easier readability after conversion as per FRE (76.9 ± 1.2 [ChatGPT-3.5] vs 66.5 ± 5.2 [Bard], p < 0.001), FKGL (5.9 ± 0.8 [ChatGPT-3.5] vs 6.9 ± 0.8 [Bard], p = 0.001), GFI (7.7 ± 0.9 [ChatGPT-3.5] vs 9.3 ± 1.0 [Bard], p < 0.001), and SMOGI (8.8 ± 0.6 [ChatGPT-3.5] vs 10.0 ± 0.8 [Bard], p < 0.001) scores (Fig. 1 ).

links.outcome: Readability grade level of AI-converted patient education materials
links.effect: Neither platform reached the recommended 6th-grade reading level; ChatGPT-3.5 converted materials to the 6th-7th grade level, while Bard converted them to the 8th-9th grade level.
links.quote: Neither platform generated PEMs written below the recommended 6th-grade reading level.
